sections.title: Basic Concept of Blood Relations
sections.content: Blood Relations questions test your ability to understand and map family relationships logically. You must carefully read statements and connect family members step by step. Never assume gender from names unless clearly mentioned. Focus only on the information provided.

sections.title: Direct Pointing to a Person
sections.content: In direct pointing questions, a person points to someone and clearly defines the relation. Example: 'He is my father.' Here, the relationship is direct and simple. Identify who is speaking and who is being pointed to before drawing conclusions.

sections.title: Indirect Pointing to a Person
sections.content: In indirect pointing, the relation is given through another person. Example: 'She is the daughter of my mother.' First identify 'my mother', then find her daughter. Break the statement into parts to avoid confusion.

sections.title: Two to Three Generation Family Tree
sections.content: These questions include grandparents, parents, and children. Example: A is the father of B. C is the sister of B. D is the mother of A. Build a small family tree step by step. This usually requires 2 to 3 logical connections.

sections.title: One-Way vs Two-Way Relationships
sections.content: A one-way relation gives information in one direction only. Example: X is the uncle of Y. This tells us about X's relation to Y. To find Y's relation to X, reverse the relation carefully. Y may be nephew or niece depending on gender. Always check gender clues before answering.

sections.title: Gender Determination Rule
sections.content: Do not assume gender from names. Use words like father, mother, sister, brother, uncle, aunt to determine gender. If gender is not given, answers may depend on both possibilities.

sections.title: Important Strategies
sections.content: 1. Draw a simple diagram. 2. Solve step by step. 3. Identify gender clearly. 4. Avoid assumptions. 5. Re-check direction of relationship before answering.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Assuming gender from names. 2. Ignoring indirect wording. 3. Not reversing relation properly in two-way questions. 4. Skipping a step in multi-generation problems.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Blood Relations questions require careful reading, diagram drawing, and logical mapping. Focus on direct and indirect pointing, two to three generation trees, and correct gender identification.

tricks.title: Family Tree Drawing Trick
tricks.explanation: Always draw a small vertical or horizontal tree to visualize relations clearly.
tricks.example: Grandparent at top, parents in middle, children at bottom.

tricks.title: Break Indirect Statements
tricks.explanation: Divide long statements into smaller parts.
tricks.example: Daughter of my mother means my sister.

tricks.title: Reverse Relation Rule
tricks.explanation: If X is uncle of Y, then Y is nephew or niece of X depending on gender.
tricks.example: If Y is female, she is niece.

tricks.title: Gender Identification First
tricks.explanation: Underline words like father, sister, uncle to confirm gender.

tricks.title: Two-Step Mapping Method
tricks.explanation: Connect A to B, then B to C to find A to C.
tricks.example: A is father of B, B is brother of C, so A is father of C.

tricks.title: Avoid Name Assumption
tricks.explanation: Do not assume gender from names unless specified.
tricks.example: Alex could be male or female unless defined.

tricks.title: Check Direction Carefully
tricks.explanation: See who is speaking and about whom.
tricks.example: He says, 'She is my aunt' – focus on speaker first.

tricks.title: Generation Gap Identification
tricks.explanation: Identify whether relation is same generation or different generation.
tricks.example: Brother is same generation, grandfather is two levels above.
